---
title: "MAGiC uncertainty training"
---

This is the uncertainty component of the MAGiC system. It runs SIPNET at design points
with the same meteorology, initial conditions, management events, and parameter priors
as the ensemble workflow, and reports which of them the modeled soil carbon and nitrous
oxide flux are most sensitive to.

Two analyses are run:

- A **local** (one-at-a-time) analysis moves each parameter in turn across its prior and
  reports each parameter's share of the parameter variance.
- A **global** (Sobol) analysis varies parameters, initial conditions, meteorology, and
  management together and reports the share of output variance from each.

Each notebook is a self-study demo to work through beforehand, then discuss in the live
session.

Topic | Audience | Objectives | Notes
--|--|--|--
[Environment setup](CARB-uncertainty-setup.md) | Everyone | Conda, AWS, and repository setup | Needed before the demo
[Uncertainty demo](uncertainty_demo.qmd) | MAGiC users | Run both analyses at two design points and read their output | Demo data covers two design points

## Commands

Command | What it does
--|--
`prepare` | Stages the ensemble inputs into `run_dir` and builds the settings of both analyses.
`local-sensitivity` | Runs the one-at-a-time analysis, computes each parameter's share of variance at each design point, and draws the figures.
`global-sensitivity` | Runs the Sobol analysis, computes the indices with bootstrap intervals at each design point, and draws the figures.

## Data flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  ENS["ensemble inputs<br/>met, initial conditions,<br/>events, priors"] --> PREP["prepare"]
  PREP --> LOC["local-sensitivity"]
  PREP --> GLO["global-sensitivity"]
```

## Audiences

Following the same roles as the [MAGiC training index](https://github.com/ccmmf/magic-training):

* **Everyone**: environment setup.
* **MAGiC users**: running the analyses and reading their output. Assumes the setup
  page is done and you are comfortable on the command line.
